_about: Batch B6b (Execution): concepts/model-runner, concepts/forward-context, concepts/attention-backends, concepts/compile-and-cuda-graphs and their module pages. Owner: the B6b writer.

persistent-batch.short: The request state that Model Runner V2 keeps on the GPU between steps, one fixed row per running request. Each step gathers its inputs from these rows.
persistent-batch.long: RequestState allocates max_num_reqs rows for token ids, lengths, computed counts, last sampled tokens and drafts ({{cite vllm/v1/worker/gpu/states.py:9-85}}). The design doc explains why the state is kept apart from the per-step inputs ({{cite docs/design/model_runner_v2.md:31-39}}).

request-slot.short: The row index that Model Runner V2 gives a request in its persistent tensors, from 0 to max_num_reqs - 1. The request keeps it until it finishes or is preempted.
request-slot.long: add_request pops a free index; remove_request appends it again, so the last freed slot is reused first ({{cite vllm/v1/worker/gpu/states.py:99-102}}, {{cite vllm/v1/worker/gpu/states.py:127-134}}).

idx-mapping.short: An int64 GPU tensor [num_reqs] that maps each row of this step's batch to the request slot in the persistent state. GPU kernels use it to gather per-request data.
idx-mapping.long: Built from the sorted request ids in gather_batch_req_state and copied to the GPU in prepare_inputs ({{cite vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py:1392-1395}}).

slot-mapping.short: For each scheduled token, the flat index of its place in the KV cache: block id × block size + offset. Padding tokens get -1 (PAD_SLOT_ID).
slot-mapping.long: Model Runner V2 computes one row per KV cache group ({{cite vllm/v1/worker/gpu/block_table.py:229-260}}); the formula is at {{cite vllm/v1/worker/gpu/block_table.py:409}}.

static-forward-context.short: A dict in the compilation config from layer name (prefix) to layer object. Attention, MoE and some other layers add themselves when they are built.
static-forward-context.long: Declared at {{cite vllm/config/compilation.py:757-760}}; the Attention layer registers at {{cite vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/attention.py:443-445}}. The forward context copies a reference to it as no_compile_layers ({{cite vllm/forward_context.py:248}}).

batch-descriptor.short: A small frozen dataclass (padded token count, request count, LoRA flags) in the forward context. Piecewise CUDA graph wrappers use it as the key of their graphs.
batch-descriptor.long: Defined at {{cite vllm/forward_context.py:29-57}}. Model Runner V2 also has its own BatchExecutionDescriptor for the dispatch decision ({{cite vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py:70-85}}).

attention-metadata.short: The per-step object that an attention backend needs to run its kernel for a group of layers: query offsets, sequence lengths, block table, slot mapping and backend-specific fields.
attention-metadata.long: A metadata builder makes it from CommonAttentionMetadata. Model Runner V2 puts it into a dict keyed by layer name ({{cite vllm/v1/worker/gpu/attn_utils.py:579-580}}).

metadata-builder.short: The AttentionMetadataBuilder of a backend. It turns the common batch description into the backend's own attention metadata, once per step for each group of layers.
metadata-builder.long: Abstract class at {{cite vllm/v1/attention/backend.py:592-761}}; the backend names it in get_builder_cls().

common-attention-metadata.short: The backend-neutral description of one step's batch for one KV cache group: query_start_loc, seq_lens, block table, slot mapping, token and request counts.
common-attention-metadata.long: Fields at {{cite vllm/v1/attention/backend.py:389-475}}. Model Runner V2 builds one per KV cache group in build_attn_metadata ({{cite vllm/v1/worker/gpu/attn_utils.py:527-548}}).

cudagraph-support.short: How much CUDA graph capture a metadata builder allows: ALWAYS, UNIFORM_BATCH, UNIFORM_SINGLE_TOKEN_DECODE or NEVER. The weakest level in the model can lower the CUDA graph mode.
cudagraph-support.long: Enum at {{cite vllm/v1/attention/backend.py:557-569}}; the runner takes the minimum over all groups ({{cite vllm/v1/worker/gpu/attn_utils.py:314-341}}).

compilation-mode.short: How vLLM applies torch.compile: NONE (eager), STOCK_TORCH_COMPILE, DYNAMO_TRACE_ONCE or VLLM_COMPILE (vLLM's own Inductor backend with graph splitting and caching).
compilation-mode.long: Enum at {{cite vllm/config/compilation.py:37-50}}. Above O0 an unset mode becomes VLLM_COMPILE ({{cite vllm/config/vllm.py:1806-1810}}).

optimization-level.short: The -O0 to -O3 switch of vllm serve. It sets defaults for the CUDA graph mode and the fusion passes; O2 is the default.
optimization-level.long: Enum at {{cite vllm/config/vllm.py:131-143}}, default at {{cite vllm/config/vllm.py:434}}, defaults per level at {{cite vllm/config/vllm.py:254-338}}.

piecewise-cuda-graph.short: CUDA graphs captured for the compiled pieces between attention ops. Attention itself runs eagerly between the replays, so any batch shape works.
piecewise-cuda-graph.long: Each compiled piece gets a CUDAGraphWrapper with runtime mode PIECEWISE ({{cite vllm/compilation/backends.py:656-707}}).

full-cuda-graph.short: One CUDA graph for the whole forward pass, attention included. Model Runner V2 replays it with a single call for batches that match a captured shape.
full-cuda-graph.long: Captured with torch.cuda.graph in CudaGraphManager.capture and replayed in run_fullgraph ({{cite vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py:555-568}}).

capture-size.short: A padded token count for which vLLM records CUDA graphs at start-up. A PIECEWISE batch runs with the smallest captured size that is not smaller than its token count.
capture-size.long: The default list is 1, 2, 4, multiples of 8 up to 248, then multiples of 16 up to the maximum ({{cite vllm/config/vllm.py:2557-2570}}).

splitting-op.short: A custom op where vLLM cuts the compiled FX graph into pieces. The op runs eagerly between the pieces, so it stays out of piecewise CUDA graphs.
splitting-op.long: By default the attention ops ({{cite vllm/config/compilation.py:768-787}}) plus the two KV cache update ops when Inductor graph partition is off ({{cite vllm/config/compilation.py:1175-1213}}).

compile-cache.short: The folder under $VLLM_CACHE_ROOT/torch_compile_cache where vLLM stores compiled graphs. A second start with the same hash loads them instead of compiling again.
compile-cache.long: The hash covers env factors, the config hash, the traced source files and the compiler ({{cite vllm/compilation/backends.py:1086-1098}}).

breakable-cuda-graph.short: An experimental way to get piecewise CUDA graphs without torch.compile: capture stops at each attention op, runs it eagerly, and starts a new graph segment.
breakable-cuda-graph.long: Module docstring {{cite vllm/compilation/breakable_cudagraph.py:3-20}}; on by default only for some architectures ({{cite vllm/config/vllm.py:75-128}}) or with VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1.
